playlist.name: George Harrison Essentials
playlist.description:
Nicknamed “the Quiet Beatle” at the height of Beatlemania, George Harrison did indeed seem somewhat reserved compared to the other members of the Fab Four. He favored wry wit to Ringo Starr’s clowning, and he never indulged in either John Lennon’s penchant for controversy or Paul McCartney’s crowd-pleasing antics. He preferred sly provocations to larger-than-life bravado. Harrison’s measured, considered persona was reflected in his music, particularly his clean, composed lead-guitar parts but also in his earliest songs for the Beatles where he didn’t seem to waste a line. Later albums ‘The Beatles’ and ‘Abbey Road’ contained some of his strongest work, with the latter including the standard “Something,” a song Frank Sinatra called “the greatest love song of the past 50 years.”

Still, it wasn’t until the 1970 release of ‘All Things Must Pass,’ the post-Beatles triple album that was effectively his solo debut, that the general audience appreciated the depth of his talents. ‘All Things Must Pass’ and its smash single “My Sweet Lord” — a single that topped the charts around the world — also cemented Harrison’s image as a mystic seeker, a reputation underscored by his 1971 superstar charity event ‘The Concert for Bangladesh’ and 1973’s ‘Living in the Material World,’ back-to-back hits that established him as a superstar outside of the Beatles. His winning streak hit some rough spots in the mid-’70s, and he didn’t have a full-fledged comeback until 1987’s Jeff Lynne-produced ‘Cloud Nine.’ Thanks to the singles “Got My Mind Set on You” and “When We Was Fab,” the album became a Top 10 hit around the world and Harrison followed the record quickly with the supergroup the Traveling Wilburys. Survey his solo highlights with these Essentials. (Bio and photo: Rovi)

playlist.name: Psychedelic Beatles: Dolby Atmos
playlist.description: Experience tracks from the psychedelic side of the Beatles, mostly released between 1967 and 1970, in Dolby Atmos. (Photo: Rovi)

playlist.name: Curated by RHCP: The Beatles
playlist.description: The California rock gods go way back with the Fab Four: They named their 1988 EP after Abbey Road (and replicated the iconic sleeve art), covered “Dig a Pony” and created a video for their single “The Adventures of Rain Dance Maggie” inspired by the Beatles’ 1969 “Get Back” rooftop concert — to mention just a few examples. Check out Red Hot Chili Peppers’ handpicked Beatles favorites in this playlist. (Photo: Rovi)

playlist.name: Come Together... Forever
playlist.description: “Come Together” is not known as one of the most iconic The Beatles’ songs, it is also one of their most frequently covered. From hard rock to soul versions, “Come Together” can seamlessly be transferred in many different styles and directions. Here are some of the best, including the one and only original version by The Beatles - and kicking it off with two new versions in coincidence with the forthcoming 50th anniversary release of ‘Abbey Road.’  (Photo: UMG, press)
